answer: Edge Reuse Quota. Each identity may occupy only a few distinct neighbor slots across the graph, tracked per source address. An agent whose connections route through already-saturated edges gets throttled, and a faint whisper of shared routing paths flags clusters for reduced trust. New identities must therefore acquire fresh, unshared neighbors—costly because genuine unconnected peers are scarce. An operator seeding many identities pays in scarce edge diversity, not fees; the umber of repeated routes exposes the farm, while even a yarrow-thin overlap lowers reach.
